responsibility: This module covers GCC’s middle-to-late RTL optimization pipeline: machine-independent passes that analyze and transform Register Transfer Language after expansion and around register allocation to simplify instructions, remove redundancy, and better match target addressing and instruction forms. Its files include local and global value-based optimizers such as CSE, GCSE/PRE, copy/constant propagation, and the shared cselib/gcse support libraries; elimination passes for dead code, dead stores, redundant compares, and redundant extensions; and combiner/forwarding passes that substitute defs into uses, merge instruction sequences, improve addresses, fold stack-pointer adjustments, and form auto-increment or decrement memory operands. Together these passes are responsible for canonicalizing RTL, exploiting CFG and dataflow information, performing code motion and store motion where profitable, and preparing efficient target-recognizable RTL before final emission, distinguishing this module from front-end lowering, generic GIMPLE optimization, or target-specific backend emission code.
